Track emissions for one pipeline step

carbon_step.Rd

Wraps a single pipeline step in a CodeCarbon task window (`tracker$start_task()` / `tracker$stop_task()`), which returns rich emissions data in memory. That data becomes the step's `carbon_log` row and is also appended to a CSV as a best-effort artifact (the CSV is never read back, so a failed write does not affect the result).

Usage

carbon_step(
  .data,
  .f,
  ...,
  tracker = carbon_default_tracker(),
  label = NULL,
  task_id = uuid::UUIDgenerate(),
  output_dir = NULL,
  output_file = NULL
)

Arguments

.data

Input data (pipe LHS).

.f

A function, or an unevaluated call whose first argument slot will receive `.data`.

...

Passed to `.f` in the function/symbol form (ignored, with a warning, in the call form — supply arguments inside the call instead).

tracker

A CodeCarbon tracker. Defaults to the session tracker registered by [carbon_init()].

label

Optional human-readable label for the step. Defaults to the deparsed `.f`.

task_id

Optional UUID string for joining/identification.

output_dir

Directory for the CSV artifact. If NULL, falls back to `tracker$output_dir` then the value registered by [carbon_init()]; if none resolves, the artifact is skipped.

output_file

CSV filename for the artifact. If NULL, falls back to the value registered by [carbon_init()] (default "emissions_r.csv").

Value

The transformed object with a `carbon_log` attribute (a rich one-row tibble of in-memory emissions data).

Details

`.f` can be supplied two ways: - **Call form** (slide syntax): `carbon_step(x, tokens_ngrams(n = 1:3))`. The unevaluated call has `.data` inserted as its first argument and is evaluated in the caller's environment. - **Function/symbol form**: `carbon_step(x, tokens, remove_punct = TRUE)`, `carbon_step(x, \(d) head(d, 3))`, `carbon_step(x, quanteda::tokens)`. The function is applied as `.f(.data, ...)`.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
carbon_init(project_name = "demo")
out <- (1:10) |> carbon_step(sqrt()) |> carbon_step(sum())
carbon_collect(out)
} # }
